title: Apple Pie by Grandma Ople
ingredients: 8 small Granny Smith apples, or as needed
instructions: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Peel and core apples, then thinly slice. Set aside.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add flour and stir to form a paste; cook until fragrant, about 1 to 2 minutes. Add both sugars and water; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Press one pastry into the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch pie pan. Roll out remaining pastry so it will overhang the pie by about 1/2 inch. Cut pastry into eight 1-inch strips.
Place sliced apples into the bottom crust, forming a slight mound. Lay four pastry strips vertically and evenly spaced over apples, using longer strips in the center and shorter strips at the edges.
Make a lattice crust: Fold back the first and third strips. Lay one of the remaining strips horizontally across the pie, then unfold the first and third strips over it.

Fold back the second and fourth vertical strips. Lay another strip horizontally across the pie, then unfold the second and fourth strips over it. Continue alternating and weaving in the remaining strips to form a lattice. Trim excess pastry as needed, then pinch the edges to seal.
Slowly pour the sugar-butter mixture over the lattice, allowing it to seep through to the apples. Brush some over the pastry, taking care not to let the mixture run over the sides.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking until the crust is golden brown, the filling is bubbling through the lattice, and the apples are tender, 35 to 45 minutes. Loosely cover the crust edges with foil if they begin to brown too quickly. Transfer the pie to a wire rack and let cool before slicing.

most_helpful_positive_review.text: My words from 2008 still hold true today. My little grandmother (and I do mean little - not more than 4' 11") would wonder what all the fuss is about - this is her recipe. Thanks to all who have commented on this little guardian angel's recipe developed years ago in her kitchen as a treat for my dad who took care of her yard and garden after my grandfather died. I am still in awe of the number of you that have tried my Grandma Ople's recipe for apple pie and love it so much. Now that she has been gone almost 15 years there seems to be less and less of her to hold on to and to pass along to her great granchildren (and great-great grandchildren) who will never know her. Some might say that having originated a delicious apple pie recipe is not much of a legacy, but when I read the reviews and notes of those who have tried her recipe, and the settings and family gatherings at which they have shared her pie, I can truly say that God has worked through my Grandmother to help bring families joy and love. Thank you all for your comments about my Grandmother's favorite recipe. Rebecca Clyma Proud Grand-daughter of Grandma Ople

featured_tweaks.text:
WONDERFUL PIE!!! I heeded other's warnings and suggestions on this one. 1. I baked the pie at 350 degreees for the entire time to minimize scorching.
2. I added 2 tablespoons flour and 1 tablespoon cornstarch to the syrup mixture. I also eliminated the water from the syrup mixture which made the pie very thick and gel-like. I also added cinnamon, cloves, allspice, and nutmeg to the syrup.
3. I mixed half of the syrup with the apples themselves before putting in the pie crust.
4. The syrup crystalizes very easily, so I made half of the syrup to mix in with the apples. Then I was able to take my time making my lattice crust and garnishes. Then, I mixed up the rest of the syrup and brushed it on the top of the pie.
5. About 10 minutes before the pie was done (about 50 minutes had elapsed), I brushed the pie with a little milk and sprinkled the top with sugar and cinnamon.
6. After making it again, I served it warm. NOT A GOOD IDEA! It was very runny. The first time allowed it to sit overnight and warmed it slightly in the microwave before serving.
I AM SO HAPPY I FOUND THIS RECIPE. I even entered it in a local pie-making contest and out of 108 entries, I recieved the grand prize and $1,000! So this is truly my award-winning pie!!! Thanks so much for the recipe! It's a keeper!

I love the flavor of this recipe, however I don't like the presentation of the top crust when done per method written. I've used this also when making a pear pie and it works ever so nicely also. I skip the 'simmer'...I just let it come to a gentle boil until the sugar is dissolved then pour over apples already placed on bottom crust. I do add a bit of apple pie spice, just personal preference; I like a bit of fall spices in my apple pie.

I have made hundreds of apple pies in my life and I believe that this is my favorite, although I changed a few things. I increased the suger, brown and white, by a half a cup, put in fresh ground cinnamon and nutmeg and vanilla. I also added a tablespoon of corn starch to the syrup mixture...it thickens the sauce better. My husband can't wait for this pie to bake. It is truely a great pie. Adding a little extra to this recipe makes it a real show stopper and my most requested pie.

I've made good apple pies for decades. :-) This is an excellent-tasting apple pie and stellar-looking as well. DON'T FORGET TO ADD CINNAMON to the sauce if you prefer your apple pie that way! I didn't realize the recipe didn't call for it until it was nearly done. :-( Also, I've never had success at getting the apples in a pie cooked all of the way through if I use more than 4 apples (I prepared 8 as this recipe calls for and ended up only using 6) and this recipe was no exception. So I placed the pie on a lower oven rack and put the temperature on 250 for an extra 30 minutes or so and that did the trick without overbaking the crust. I used the Basic Flaky Pie Crust recipe from this website and it was excellent.

This is an excellent recipe. I double the butter/sugar sauce mixture and after removing it form heat added 1tsp cinnamon & 1 tsp vanilla. I also mixed the apples in the sauce before filling the pie shell. I made 12 mini apple pies using a muffin tray & puff pastry. They looked awesome. I added chopped walnuts in half of them and they were the best! Thanks for sharing.

I never leave reviews, but this pie deserves one. So much fun to make, and so tasty! This is my third or fourth time making this pie. This time, I followed someone else’s suggestion to stir most of the caramel sauce and a Tbsp of cinnamon into the apple slices, and pour the remaining sauce over the lattice. I also egg washed the bottom shell, to try and keep it from getting soggy, and egg washed the lattice and edges before adding the caramel sauce. It looks great! I haven’t tasted it yet - saving it for Thanksgiving tomorrow! Also, if you include preparing the apples, this takes much more than 30 mins to prep (unless you have a peeler/corer/slicer). But it’s worth it! Thanks for sharing this tasty recipe!

I used this for a base to a incredible pie. Mine had a solid top crust and I added lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, vanilla and cornstarch to the golden delicious apples before covering them in the sugar/caramel mix. Coated the top crust with egg white and sugar. One of the best I've ever made.

Perfection!! Turned out absolutely perfect. I prepared the apple pie filling ahead of time by sautéing in a pan in the butter and until fork tender but still retaining shape. Then added sugar and spices (Cinnamon, dash of nutmeg and dash of cloves), then took off the heat and added apple cider instead of water, and lemon juice. I reserved some liquid to pour over the crust. I cooked it about 50 min until crust was finished. Lattice top crust is a must, so filling is not too much liquid. It was the best apple pie I ever had! :-) UPDATE: 6 apples seem to work better than 8. There wasn't enough crust to apple ratio for my taste with 8 by a long shot. Bottom crust was not crispy enough...maybe prebake next time? It's been too soupy a few times so next time I will be sure to add more flour or use less liquid. Still delicious though.

Loved the base of this recipe. I added some cinnamon to the sugar mixture and layered the apples with the mixture instead of pouring it all on top. Also, used an egg wash for the top. It all worked out perfectly!

This was the best pie I've made in years! I used Serious Eats Easy pie dough. 6 small Granny Smiths and 2 large golden delicious (about 8 cups, thinly sliced by a Yankee apple peeling gizmo). I added a about 1/8 tsp of salt, a teaspoon of cinnamon, and an overflowing teaspoon of vanilla to the caramel after taking it off the stove. Poured 3/4 caramel into the bowl of sliced apples and brushed the remainder of the syrup onto the top crust. So delicious the 3 of us finished it in record time. So I baked another!
